prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map depicts a downward-sloping muddy trail where the camera wearer's white hat brim at the bottom center (frames 2–5) and extended left arm at the bottom left (frames 1–3) appear brightest at roughly 0.1–0.7 m, while the ground drops away from about 1.5 m beneath the wearer's feet to over 4 m toward the upper-right sky and vegetation. In frame 1, a person in light blue stands 1–1.5 m directly ahead on a wooden plank with their upper body cropped out at the top edge, whereas in frames 2–3 a second person in grey trousers and a dark jacket stands 1.5–2.5 m ahead on the slope, approaches to within arm's reach (under 1 m) as their right hand clasps the wearer's left hand in frame 3, and is replaced in frames 4–5 by a person in a blue poncho carrying a yellow hat/bag at 2–3 m on the right and another crouching person further upslope to the upper left at 3–4 m (roughly 1.5–2 m apart from each other). All visible people have their heads cropped or obscured near the top border, with the person in frames 2–3 facing toward the camera wearer down the slope and the poncho-clad person in frames 4–5 angled slightly left toward the trail. Compared to RGB, the depth map clearly separates the foreground silhouettes of the overlapping hands in frame 3 and the hanging yellow object in frame 5 from the cluttered mud and grass background. However, it is unreliable where the bright white hat brim saturates to uniform near-zero depth, fine grassy vegetation blurs into smooth gradients, and the upper-right sky/horizon collapses into a flat black void.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates foreground people and objects against a black background across the sloped trail, labeling the primary person standing 1–3 m in front of and below the camera wearer as 'person' (pink mask) in all five frames, while all heads remain cropped above the top frame edge. It separates the camera wearer's own extended left arm in the lower left of frames 2 and 3 (within 0.7 m) as a distinct brown 'person' mask that approaches and touches the pink person's right hand at arm's reach in frame 3 before disappearing below the frame in frames 4–5. In frames 4 and 5, it also detects the lower legs and hands of another person crouching 3–4 m away in the upper left (blue and light-green 'person' masks, about 1.5–2 m left of the pink person), revealing that background hiker's presence much more clearly than the camouflaged muddy RGB background. However, the map is unreliable in class labels and completeness: it misclassifies the camera wearer's white hat brim (at 0.1–0.3 m in the bottom foreground) as a blue 'frisbee' in frames 2 and 5 while missing it entirely in frames 3 and 4, and it mislabels the yellow hat/bag hanging at the right person's hip (at ~2.5 m) as a purple 'frisbee' in frames 4 and 5. It also fails to segment the wearer's black sleeve in frame 1, another person's blue hood in the lower-right corner of frame 4, and the entire terrain.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders 2D body skeletons (yellow) and hand skeletons (magenta) on a black canvas, tracking the limb orientations of the people standing 1.5–3 m in front of the camera wearer in frames 2–5 while detecting nothing in frame 1. In frame 2, the person ~2 m ahead faces the camera wearer with torso, legs, both arms, and cropped neck/head keypoints visible, and the wearer's own outstretched left hand is captured in magenta at the bottom left within 0.6 m, clarifies finger articulation against the dark mud better than RGB. In frame 3, as the person approaches to ~1 m and grasps the wearer's hand, the pose estimator becomes highly unreliable, collapsing the person's legs and torso into a tangled cluster near their right wrist and missing the wearer's arm and both clasped hands completely. As the next person in the blue poncho stands 2–3 m ahead to the right in frames 4 and 5, the skeleton tracks their straight legs and torso shifting rightward and turning slightly toward the camera wearer, registering a magenta right-hand skeleton at their hip in frame 5 within reach of their yellow bag. Across all frames, the map fails to detect the upper-left crouching person (3–4 m away), any part of the person in frame 1, or reliable head/gaze keypoints for people cropped by the top border.
